classification.difficultyReason: Solve two inequalities with negative coefficients and intersect their solution sets.

content.prompt: Suppose that $x$ satisfies both $15-2x<2$ and $15-2x>-2$. Solve for $x$, showing your answer on a number line.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}15-2x&<2\\-2x&<-13\\\frac{-2x}{-2}&>\frac{-13}{-2}\\x&>\frac{13}{2}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}15-2x&>-2\\-2x&>-17\\\frac{-2x}{-2}&<\frac{-17}{-2}\\x&<\frac{17}{2}\end{align*}$$
Reverse each inequality when dividing by $-2$. Both conditions hold when $\dfrac{13}{2}<x<\dfrac{17}{2}$. The endpoints are excluded.

spec.description: Authored solution number line with an open interval segment above the axis. TikZ is used because the supplied number-line template does not specify interval segments between open endpoints.
spec.mathematics: All real x strictly between 13/2 and 17/2; both endpoint circles are open.
